finding: Spherical gas-fueled cool diffusion flames (CDFs) were observed for the first time on the ISS, specifically for normal n-butane flames at 2 bar (~29 psi) and XO2 = 0.39 (39% O2); the hot flames that spawned them were 2.6x larger.

Inverse spherical diffusion flames issued up to 85% O2 (balance N2) from the 6.35-mm burner into ethane, propane, and n-butane mixtures at 7.35 to 44.1 psia — the highest oxygen concentration tested in PSI combustion flight datasets.

Exposed platinum in fine Type-B thermocouples (~1 cm from burner) catalytically triggered repeated hot-flame reignition from cool flames, proving invisible cool flames can reignite into full hot fires on catalytic surfaces.

Companion stagnation-flow n-heptane cool diffusion flames measured peak temperatures of 705–760 K (autoignition onset 550 K) with formaldehyde emissions, well below Cantera homogeneous predictions of 885 K.

Liquid alkane droplets (n-heptane, n-octane, n-decane, n-dodecane) radiative-extinguish from visible hot flames (~1500–2000 K) into sustained invisible cool flames (~500–800 K) producing CO and formaldehyde until vapor-accumulation reignition or diffusive extinction.
